Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows extensive opacification of the right hemithorax with a distinct, abnormally elevated (superiorly displaced) horizontal fissure, which is a classic radiographic sign of right lung torsion causing venous congestion and hemorrhagic infarction. This specific finding distinguishes it from simple effusion or pneumonia where the fissure would typically be depressed or normally positioned, respectively.
